day.headline: Sensex fell 460 points and Nifty 0.54% for a third straight loss as Brent jumped above $110 on fresh West Asia attacks and FIIs sold ₹3,459 cr.
day.summary: Houthi drone strikes on Saudi Arabia's Shaybah oilfield and Dammam airport pushed Brent crude above $110, reviving inflation worries for oil-importing India. Mid- and smallcaps fell harder than the benchmarks (Midcap 100 at a six-month low), while domestic institutions bought ₹2,891 cr to absorb heavy foreign selling. Pharma and PSU banks were the rare gainers; IT, FMCG and media led the declines ahead of Infosys results.

items.title: Sensex −460 pts, Nifty −124 pts as Brent tops $110 on Saudi oilfield attack
items.why: Equity fund NAVs slipped for a third day, with mid/smallcap funds hit harder than large-cap ones. Benchmarks fell after Houthi drone strikes on Saudi Arabia's Shaybah oilfield and Dammam airport lifted December Brent 1.85% to $110.83; higher oil raises India's import bill, pressures the rupee and stokes inflation.

items.title: FIIs sell ₹3,458.70 cr; DIIs buy ₹2,891.32 cr in cash market
items.why: Domestic buying (largely mutual fund SIP money) cushioned the fall, a useful talking point for clients worried about foreign outflows. FIIs (foreign institutional investors) swung from net buyers of ₹1,022.32 cr on 21/10 to heavy sellers; figures are provisional exchange data.

items.title: Midcap 100 hits six-month low; smallcaps fall 1.14%, breadth weak
items.why: Mid- and smallcap fund investors are seeing the sharpest drawdowns in this correction, so expect queries; investors are cutting riskier positions first. Midcap 100 fell 0.87% and Smallcap 100 1.14% (NSE data; one source shows −1.17%), while 38 of 50 Nifty stocks closed lower.

items.title: Swiggy Q2: loss narrows to ₹922 cr, revenue up 36.1% to ₹7,571 cr
items.why: Swiggy sits in many new-age/consumption and midcap fund portfolios, and the market judged these numbers weak the next day (stock −16% on 23/10). Results came out on 22/10; the stock already fell 5.48% that session.

items.title: Indian Hotels +3.89% on strong earnings; KEI Industries −8.45% on margin worries
items.why: Results season is moving individual holdings sharply, which shows up in sector and midcap fund NAVs. Indian Hotels rose on strong earnings and tourism stocks led sectors (+1.10%), while KEI fell over margin concerns; Colgate-Palmolive posted 4.2% profit growth to ₹342 cr with margins narrowing to 28% from 31%.

items.title: ZFunds launches US stocks and ETFs, opens 5,000 accounts on day one
items.why: Distributor platforms are adding direct overseas investing, which competes with international fund-of-funds for client money. ZFunds (an MFD platform) said it opened 5,000 accounts on launch day.
